item.title: [EN|In-Depth] BBC Global News Podcast (Sun 22:00): The Global Story: AI can imitate a human. But can it think like one?
item.description:
Originally published Sun 22 Nov 2026 22:00 IST.

For decades, computer scientists have been trying to figure out whether computers can think. But with the advent of highly sophisticated chatbots like Claude and ChatGPT…might we finally have our answer? This week we’re introducing The Global Backstory, the new strand of our show that explores the history behind the news today. We constantly hear stories about artificial intelligence, but most of them are about where AI is going; in this five-episode series we’re looking at where it came from. Beginning with computer scientist Alan Turing’s famous Turing test in 1950, the quest to verify the existence of machine intelligence has taken on many forms – from the rudimentary chatbots of the 1960s, to the 1997 defeat of a chess grand master by a computer, to IBM Watson’s stint on Jeopardy in the 2010s. But large language models have rendered old methods of measuring machine intelligence obsolete. So how smart is AI, anyway? And will it ever be smarter than us? Tristan Redman and Asma Khalid are joined by Thomas Germain, BBC technology columnist and host of the BBC podcast The Interface. The Global Story brings clarity to politics, business and foreign policy in a time of connection and disruption. For more episodes, just search 'The Global Story' wherever you get your BBC Podcasts.
